increment: Fresh directional capacity review for manual main-order sizing

prd.title: Futures trading
requirements: 输入一笔开仓订单后，分别预估买卖两侧；同一输入可能只满足一侧。
超过上限时提示该方向最新最大可下金额，并保留原输入。
点击买卖按钮时重新核对该侧数量和最新额度；确认页保持相同交易对、方向、订单类型与数量。

implemented: Manual base/quote sizing now uses the shared fresh capacity preparation, frozen confirmation, submit guard and original-ID recovery for non-pegged LIMIT, Post Only, MARKET, STOP/TAKE_PROFIT limit/market and TRAILING_STOP_MARKET opening orders. Reducing flows remain on their dedicated path.

Without a previous capacity read, manual input can produce an independently validated per-side quantity preview and enable the corresponding review action. It does not invent a maximum or cost. Only an explicit review or read starts private requests.

Both manual directional buttons and the existing main review action capture the selected side and exact resolved base quantity before refreshing capacity. At most five signatures re-read account facts; larger capacity never enlarges that captured quantity.

A fresh over-capacity result carries the selected-side latest maximum and context into a localized error. Base/quote units follow the form; quote maxima remain approximate. Raw entered strings survive failure, cancellation, wallet rejection and accepted placement; percentage placement retains its existing zero-reset behavior.

Side-specific filters can enable only one action for a shared input. Pre-wallet and after-wallet guards reject observed identity, symbol, context, form, capacity, clock, settings and recovery changes. Unknown submission retains the original ID and never issues a second POST.

Review actions disable during preparation, with a spinner on the clicked directional action and main review control. Main review now respects its enabled flag while capacity is being read. Text labels remain available while pending.

Shared production-form test fixture serves manual and percentage widget tests. Legacy retry test scrolls the expanded form before tapping again; missing-price coverage explicitly checks that only the affected direction is disabled.

coverage: Six inline modes in both directions; raw base input; independent MARKET quote conversion; no prerequisite explicit capacity read.
Latest maxima in EN/ZH and both units; retry after exceeded capacity; growing limits do not resize; only-one-side-valid input.
Manual main review uses the same guard; cancel during read; loading controls; wallet rejection; separate raw base/quote strings; skip-confirmation; unknown original-ID query.
EN/ZH narrow portrait, landscape and tablet with 1.5x text; semantics remain enabled.
After-wallet form/clock/symbol/stale/capacity invalidation; exact real repository POST and signed query terms in six modes and both directions; journal persistence and GET-only unknown recovery.

remaining_required_work: Continuous public-price/account-event recomputation and reconnection snapshots; current sizing still uses bounded preflight and signed facts.
Independent post-trade liquidation estimates in applicable account/margin/position modes.
Verified reservation amounts for pending conditional, MARKET and moving BBO orders. Unknown inputs continue to block capacity calculation.
Moving BBO has no verified pricing contract for the new capacity guard. Its existing dedicated preflight/signing path remains; this increment does not claim full capacity coverage for it.
Other PRD gaps and product/protocol scope clarifications remain in docs/prd-progress.md; only historical statistics/Summary/TWAP are user-deferred.
boundaries: Capacity and cost are estimates, not guarantees of API authorization, order acceptance, fill price or spending cap. No fees or future released margin are credited by the opening-cost kernel.
The five signed reads are not an atomic snapshot; guards protect against observed changes and expiry, not unobserved exchange state after the last response.
Tests use synthetic responses. No real private/funds/chat request, wallet signature or address-bearing RPC is performed for this increment.
User deferred device verification; no device tools, app install or publication. Linux lacks macOS/Xcode for iOS builds.
